title: [Mellanox][Smartswitch] Add blacklist for dpu kernel module to prevent race condition
body:
<!--
     Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines:
     https://github.com/Azure/SONiC/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md

     ** Make sure all your commits include a signature generated with `git commit -s` **

     If this is a bug fix, make sure your description includes "fixes #xxxx", or
     "closes #xxxx" or "resolves #xxxx"

     Please provide the following information:
-->

#### Why I did it

On this Mellanox SmartSwitch platform, the `mlxreg_dpu` kernel module needs to be loaded only after the platform's I2C topology is in place, and is loaded explicitly later in boot. The current modprobe.d-based blacklist that gates early autoload is written by a userspace service and is subject to a race against udev-driven autoload on early boot, which intermittently causes `mlxreg_dpu` to attach too early. Adding the blacklist via the kernel command line in `installer.conf` makes the gate effective from PID 0, closing the race while still allowing the later explicit `modprobe` to load the module normally.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

Append `modprobe.blacklist=mlxreg_dpu` to `ONIE_PLATFORM_EXTRA_CMDLINE_LINUX` in the platform `installer.conf`. ONIE bakes this into the GRUB `linux` line at install time, so the parameter is present on the kernel command line from the very first boot.

```1:1:device/mellanox/x86_64-nvidia_sn4280-r0/installer.conf
ONIE_PLATFORM_EXTRA_CMDLINE_LINUX="libata.force=noncq ima_hash=sha384 amd_iommu=off cpufreq.default_governor=performance modprobe.blacklist=mlxreg_dpu"
```

The canonical module name `mlxreg_dpu` (underscore — as reported by `modinfo`'s `name:` field, even though the on-disk object is `mlxreg-dpu.ko`) is used so that `kmod` matches the autoload alias. Explicit `modprobe mlxreg-dpu` calls later in boot are unaffected, since `modprobe.blacklist=` only suppresses implicit/alias/dependency loads.

#### How to verify it

On a freshly installed image of the affected platform:

1. Confirm the kernel command line carries the blacklist:

    ```
    cat /proc/cmdline | tr ' ' '\n' | grep modprobe.blacklist
    # expect: modprobe.blacklist=mlxreg_dpu
    ```

2. Confirm the explicit modprobe path still loads the module during normal boot:

    ```
    lsmod | grep mlxreg_dpu
    # expect: mlxreg_dpu loaded (loaded later in boot via explicit modprobe)
    ```

3. Functional verification: run the SmartSwitch DPU bring-up sanity test across repeated cold boots and confirm the DPUs reach the expected operational state — the previous race manifested as intermittent failures in this scenario.

title: [vnetorch] Resolve interface for directly-connected local endpoints
body:
## What I did

For VNET routes using `custom_bfd` monitoring, resolve the RIF interface alias for **directly-connected local endpoints** before calling `NeighOrch::hasNextHop` / `getNextHopId` / ref-count APIs. Applied symmetrically in both the single-NH path (`createNextHopGroup`) and the multi-NH path (`addNextHopGroup`).

## Why I did it

VNET routes with `monitoring=custom_bfd` whose **primary** endpoint is a directly-connected local DPU IP fail to install. The route stays in `inactive` state in `STATE_DB` even when:

- The BFD session is `Up` and a notification reaches vnetorch
- The kernel ARP table has the neighbor as `REACHABLE`
- `APP_DB:NEIGH_TABLE:<intf>:<DPU-IP>` exists (NeighOrch has the neighbor as `IP@<intf>`)

### Root cause

The `NextHopGroupKey` for VNET routes is constructed from `VNET_ROUTE_TUNNEL_TABLE.endpoint`, which only carries IPs (no interface). For directly-connected local endpoints the `NextHopKey` carries an **empty alias** (`<IP>@`). The lookup `NeighOrch::hasNextHop(<IP>@<empty>)` misses the stored entry `<IP>@<intf>`, and `createNextHopGroup` returns `false`:

```
NOTICE swss#orchagent: createNextHopGroup: Next hop 100.117.156.35@ not found in neighorch, skipping.
WARNING swss#orchagent: updateVnetTunnelCustomMonitor: Failed to create primary based custom next hop group. Cannot proceed.
```

Note the empty alias after the `@`. The corresponding APP_DB entry is properly keyed:

```
$ redis-cli -n 0 keys '*NEIGH*' | grep 100.117.156.35
NEIGH_RESOLVE_TABLE:Vlan32:100.117.156.35
NEIGH_TABLE:Vlan32:100.117.156.35
```

So NeighOrch stores `100.117.156.35@Vlan32` while vnetorch looks up `100.117.156.35@<empty>`.

The Down path (`NeighOrch::updateNextHop`, triggered by `BfdUpdate`) correctly resolves the alias and logs `setNextHopFlag on <IP> seen on port Vlan32`. This PR brings the create/Up path to parity.

### Related

Companion fix on the HA-manager / producer side: [sonic-net/sonic-dash-ha#152](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dash-ha/pull/152) (adds interface name to `NEIGH_RESOLVE_TABLE` keys for VLAN interfaces). That PR ensures the neighbor gets resolved with the correct interface. **This PR closes the consumer-side gap** so vnetorch can find the resolved neighbor.

## How I verified it

Tested in lab:

Primary: 
~$  redis-cli -n 6   hgetall "VNET_ROUTE_TUNNEL_TABLE|Vnet_55|3.2.1.0/32"
1) "active_endpoints"
2) "20.0.200.1"
3) "state"
4) "active"

Secondary 
:~$  redis-cli -n 6   hgetall "VNET_ROUTE_TUNNEL_TABLE|Vnet_55|3.2.1.0/32"
1) "active_endpoints"
2) "10.1.0.32"
3) "state"
4) "active"

## Details if related

This bug only manifests in the `custom_bfd` monitoring code path that goes through `updateCustomBfdState` → `selectNextHopGroup` → `createNextHopGroup`. The non-monitoring path is unaffected because it builds `NextHopKey` with the interface already resolved upstream.

The fix uses `NeighOrch::getNeighborEntry(IpAddress, NeighborEntry&, MacAddress&)`, which is the existing API for IP-to-alias resolution. The resolution is conditional on `isLocalEp && alias.empty()` so it has no effect on non-local endpoints or cases where the alias was already populated.

Signed-off-by: zhangjing <zhangjing@microsoft.com>

title: [platform_tests][T2] Add test_sup_fan_recovery.py to verify sup fan status after config reload + cold reboot
body:
<!--
Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines;
https://github.com/sonic-net/SONiC/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md

Please provide following information to help code review process a bit easier:
-->
### Description of PR
<!--
- Please include a summary of the change and which issue is fixed.
- Please also include relevant motivation and context. Where should reviewer start? background context?
- List any dependencies that are required for this change.
-->

Summary:
Adds a new T2 chassis platform test `tests/platform_tests/test_sup_fan_recovery.py` that exercises the supervisor (sup) recovery path after a `config load_minigraph --override_config` followed by a cold reboot, and asserts that every fan on the sup comes back in `OK` state.
The test targets a thermalctld / psu-service issue where, after a sup reload + cold reboot, fans were intermittently reported as `Not present` by `show platform fan` and thermalctld emitted `UnboundLocalError` tracebacks in syslog (with associated `Fan removed warning` / `Insufficient number of working fans` messages).

Fixes # (issue)

### Type of change

<!--
- Fill x for your type of change.
- e.g.
- [x] Bug fix
-->

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ X] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [ ] Test case improvement


### Back port request
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ X] 202511
- [ ] 202512
- [ ] 202605

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
After a chassis sup is reloaded with `config load_minigraph --override_config -y` and then cold rebooted, thermalctld occasionally came back in a broken state: `show platform fan` reported one or more fans as `Not present`, and syslog showed `UnboundLocalError` tracebacks plus `Fan removed warning` / `Insufficient number of working fans` messages. There was no automated regression coverage for this sup-specific recovery path, so the bug was caught only manually. This PR adds that coverage.


#### How did you do it?
Added `tests/platform_tests/test_sup_fan_recovery.py` containing `test_sup_fan_status_after_reload_reboot`. The test is scoped to `t2` (via `pytest.mark.topology('t2')`) and iterates over `duthosts.supervisor_nodes`. For each sup it:
1. Snapshots `/var/core/` on every DUT (sup + linecards).
2. Skips cleanly if `/etc/sonic/minigraph.xml` is not present on the sup (cannot run `load_minigraph`).
3. Arms a sup-scoped `LogAnalyzer` with match regexes for the bug signature:
   - `Traceback (most recent call last)`
   - `UnboundLocalError`
   - `Fan removed warning`
   - `Insufficient number of working fans`
4. Runs `config_reload(sup, config_source='minigraph', override_config=True, wait=420)` — equivalent to `sudo config load_minigraph --override_config -y`.
5. Calls `test_reboot.reboot_and_check(..., reboot_type=REBOOT_TYPE_COLD, duthosts=duthosts)`, which also runs `check_interfaces_and_services` on the sup and every frontend linecard.
6. Polls `show platform fan` on the sup for up to 90 s and **fails if any fan is not `OK`** — stricter than the upstream `check_fan_status` helper (which accepts `>=1` OK fan), because the bug is specifically about one or more fans being incorrectly non-OK.
7. Runs `sup_la.analyze(...)` so any of the listed tracebacks/warnings between the markers fail the test.
8. After all sups are processed, asserts no new core dumps appeared on any card during the test.


#### How did you verify/test it?
- Ran on a T2 chassis testbed against a build that reproduces the bug — test fails on the fan-status assertion and the LogAnalyzer flags the `UnboundLocalError` traceback, as expected.
- Ran on a T2 chassis testbed against a fixed build — test passes; all fans `OK`, no matching syslog entries, no new core dumps.
- Confirmed graceful skips:
  - Non-chassis / no `supervisor_nodes` → `pytest.skip(...)`.
  - Sup without `/etc/sonic/minigraph.xml` → `pytest.skip(...)`.
  - `asic_type == "vs"` and `switch_type == "dpu"` → `_all_fans_ok` returns `True`.
#### Any platform specific information?
T2 modular chassis only (requires a real supervisor card with fans reported by `show platform fan`). Non-T2 topologies are excluded by `pytest.mark.topology('t2')`, and within T2 the test self-skips on virtual switch / DPU and when no sup minigraph is present.
#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?
T2

#### Why I did it

Update the Nvidia BlueField DPU SONiC build to the latest NASA / SAI (`NASA 26.4-RC4` / `SAIBuild 0.0.53.0`) and bring in the accompanying tuning, build, and runtime fixes required to make the new stack usable.

Specifically:
- Reserve 14 cores on the DPU for NASA for higher performance in Data path
- Bump DPDK mbuf headroom to 256 bytes in the DPU DPDK build to match encap requirements of Inline Sync in HA
- Update SAI TCP / UDP aging intervals to 300s / 120s
- Move DPU SAI / SDK recipes to `NASA 26.4-RC4` and `SAIBuild 0.0.53.0`.
- Clean up stale DPDK/SDN patches that no longer apply against the new NASA DPDK source
- Switch `dpuctlplat` to unbind/bind the DPU PCI devices instead of the previous rescan-based flow. This makes DPU power / reset transitions more reliable.
- Add `openibd` service installation and related config wiring in `sonic_debian_extension.j2` so IB / RDMA verbs come up correctly on the DPU image.

title: Skip Redis client init for DBs not in database_config.json
body:
<!--
     Please make sure you've read and understood our contributing guidelines:
     https://github.com/Azure/SONiC/blob/gh-pages/CONTRIBUTING.md

     ** Make sure all your commits include a signature generated with `git commit -s` **

     If this is a bug fix, make sure your description includes "fixes #xxxx", or
     "closes #xxxx" or "resolves #xxxx"

     Please provide the following information:
-->

#### Why I did it
`initRedisDbClients()` and `useRedisTcpClient()` iterate over every entry in the `spb.Target_value` proto enum and call `sdcfg.GetDbSock` / `sdcfg.GetDbTcpAddr` for each one. When a `Target` enum value corresponds to a DB that is not present in the device's database_config.json (e.g. DPU_COUNTERS_DB on a non-smartswitch / non-DPU platform), the underlying `SonicDBConfig::getDbInfo` call logs an ERR-level message to syslog:

 ```
ERR gnmi#telemetry: :- getDbInfo: Failed to find DPU_COUNTERS_DB database in : key
 ERR gnmi#dialout_client_cli: :- getDbInfo: Failed to find DPU_COUNTERS_DB database in : key
```

This was introduced as a side-effect of adding `DPU_COUNTERS_DB = 18` to the `Target` enum. Since `DPU_COUNTERS_DB` is only configured on smartswitch / DPU platforms, every other platform now emits these benign ERR logs every time `gnmi / dialout_client_cli` starts up.
#### How I did it
- Added a helper `configuredDbSet(dbNamespace)` that returns the set of DB names actually present in `database_config.json` for the given namespace.
 - In both `useRedisTcpClient()` (TCP path) and `initRedisDbClients()` (UNIX socket path), look up the configured DB set before iterating `spb.Target_value`. If a Target enum entry isn't in the configured set, skip it with a `V(2)` info log instead of calling `sdcfg.GetDbSock` / `sdcfg.GetDbTcpAddr` and triggering the ERR.

title: [dash]: add dash scale performance tests for dash programming
body:
### Description of PR

**Summary:** Add DASH scale programming tests that measure the end-to-end gNMI → orchagent → SAI pipeline performance for routes and VNET mappings on SmartSwitch DPUs.

Two new tests in `tests/dash/test_dash_scale.py`:

1. **`test_combined_scale_programming_time`** — Programs 10K routes + 10K VNET mappings under a single ENI, validates all APPL_STATE_DB results are written with `result=0`, measures gNMI and SAI throughput, then deletes all objects and validates removal.

2. **`test_multi_eni_scale_programming_time`** — Programs 4 ENIs each with 2500 routes + 2500 mappings (20K total), validating multi-ENI scale correctness and gNMI throughput.

Both tests report detailed metrics: gNMI send time, sairedis.rec SAI programming timestamps, and syncd syslog bulkCreate cycle analysis.

### Type of change
- [x] New Test case
    - [x] Skipped for non-supported platforms

### Approach

#### What is the motivation for this PR?
Establish baseline performance measurements and regression guards for DASH scale programming on SmartSwitch. There were no existing tests that measured how long it takes to program large numbers of DASH routes and VNET mappings via gNMI, or that validated the full pipeline from gNMI SET through orchagent SAI programming to APPL_STATE_DB result confirmation.

#### How did you do it?
- Created test_dash_scale.py with configurable scale parameters (`--num_scale_routes`, `--num_scale_vnet_mappings`, `--num_scale_enis`)
- Config ordering follows `test_fnic.py`: appliance/VNET/route group → routes/mappings → route rules → ENI → ENI route group binding
- Primary validation: APPL_STATE_DB result entries with `result=0` for all programmed objects
- Secondary metrics: sairedis.rec timestamps for SAI wall time, syncd syslog parsing for bulkCreate cycle analysis
- Throughput thresholds (10% tolerance): gNMI ≥ 540 obj/s, SAI ≥ 720 obj/s (single ENI only)
- Added `conftest.py` options: `--num_scale_routes` (default 10000), `--num_scale_vnet_mappings` (default 10000), `--scale_poll_timeout` (default 600), `--num_scale_enis` (default 4)

#### How did you verify/test it?
Ran both tests on a SmartSwitch testbed with DPU. Results:
- Combined test (create): 20K objects programmed, gNMI ~600 obj/s, SAI routes ~842 obj/s, SAI mappings ~856 obj/s, 100% result validation pass
- Combined test (delete): 20K objects removed, gNMI throughput validated
- Multi-ENI test: 4 ENIs × 5K objects each, gNMI ~615 obj/s, all results validated

#### Any platform specific information?
SmartSwitch platforms with DPU modules only.

`smartswitch`

title: [module_base] Record DPU reboot time at command invocation
body:
#### Description

Write `prev_reboot_time.txt` from `module_base.py` when `reboot()` or `set_admin_state(down)` is issued, rather than relying solely on chassisd to write it when it detects the Online→Offline transition.

Changes:
- Add `_record_dpu_reboot_time()` helper to `ModuleBase` that writes the current UTC timestamp to `/host/reboot-cause/module/{module}/prev_reboot_time.txt`
- Add `reboot_gracefully(reboot_type)` wrapper that records the reboot time then calls `reboot()`
- Call `_record_dpu_reboot_time()` in `set_admin_state_gracefully(up=False)` at the start of the down path
- Add unit tests for the new methods

#### Motivation and Context

There is a race condition in the current DPU reboot-cause persistence flow: if `config reload` is issued shortly after `reboot -d DPUX`, chassisd restarts before it can detect the Online→Offline transition and write `prev_reboot_time.txt`. When chassisd comes back, it sees EMPTY→Offline and has no reboot time to compare against, potentially losing the reboot event.

By writing `prev_reboot_time.txt` at the moment the user issues the reboot/shutdown command (in `module_base`), the timestamp is already persisted before any race can occur. Chassisd's existing write during Online→Offline detection is preserved as a fallback for spontaneous DPU crashes (not user-initiated).

Related PR: sonic-net/sonic-platform-daemons#771

#### How Has This Been Tested?

1. Unit tests — all 5 new test cases pass:
   - `test_record_dpu_reboot_time_success` — verifies file creation and format
   - `test_record_dpu_reboot_time_failure` — verifies graceful error handling
   - `test_reboot_gracefully_records_time_then_reboots` — verifies wrapper calls both methods
   - `test_reboot_gracefully_still_reboots_on_time_record_failure` — verifies reboot proceeds on time-write failure
   - `test_set_admin_state_gracefully_down_records_time` — verifies admin-down calls `_record_dpu_reboot_time`
   - `test_set_admin_state_gracefully_up_does_not_record_time` — verifies admin-up does NOT record time

2. Existing `module_base_test.py` tests updated to patch `_record_dpu_reboot_time` in down-path tests — all continue to pass.

#### Additional Information (Optional)

This change is complementary to sonic-net/sonic-platform-daemons#771. The two writes are safe to coexist:

| Scenario | module_base writes | chassisd writes |
|---|---|---|
| `reboot -d DPU0` (normal) | ✅ at command time | ✅ at Online→Offline detection |
| `reboot -d DPU0` + `config reload` (race) | ✅ at command time | ❌ missed (chassisd restarted) |
| Spontaneous DPU crash | ❌ (no command) | ✅ at Online→Offline detection |
